open_issues: The literal command 'dotnet test tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests --no-dependencies' given in the brief fails with MSBUILD error MSB1001 ('Unknown switch') under this repo's pinned SDK (10.0.401) — .NET 10's 'dotnet test' front-end no longer accepts --no-dependencies (confirmed via 'dotnet test --help': the switch is gone from the VSTest-bridge command). I substituted the equivalent, dependency-safe sequence 'dotnet build tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests --no-dependencies' followed by 'dotnet test tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests --no-build', which builds only the test project (using Wakeel.UI's and Wakeel.Core's already-built outputs, never rebuilding them) and then runs the already-built test binary. All three required commands (Wakeel.UI build, Wakeel.Desktop build, and this test sequence) are green. Flagging in case the orchestrator's own verification step still uses the original literal command and needs the same substitution.

I did not do a fresh pixel-measurement pass against every reference PNG (W08, W01, W91, W92, W20 and their dark twins) in this session — the design system, shell, and W08 placeholder page already existed in the working tree (evidently from an earlier session, per the repo's own memory notes on 'Al-Wakeel design phase state') using the 8px grid / radius 6/10/pill / 38px control height / 44px row conventions the guide specifies. I verified structural conformance (logical-only CSS properties, RTL, token usage, icon inventory, Desktop host requirements) rather than re-deriving every measurement from the images myself; if pixel-level fidelity regressions are suspected, a dedicated visual diff against the PNGs would be the next step.
notes:
This work package (src/Wakeel.UI, src/Wakeel.Desktop, tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests) was already substantially implemented in the working tree when I started — full token/app CSS, bundled Noto Sans Arabic woff2 (4 weights, real ~50KB files with OFL license), a vendored Lucide icon set (all names from the spec present, using chevron-left/right/up/down + chevrons-left-right to cover the generic 'chevrons' entry), every listed component (WButton..Kbd) each as .razor + scoped .razor.css, MainLayout/Bidi/Ar.cs/ThemeService/Gallery/W08AttentionCenter, and a WPF Desktop host (Serilog with ProgramData→LocalAppData fallback, WebView2 user-data folder under LocalAppData, file-based IUiStateStore, --remote-debugging-port forwarding via WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS, 1366x768 window min 1200x700, FlowDirection=RightToLeft, start route '/' redirecting to '/gallery').

My session's actual work was bringing the build+test pipeline from broken to fully green:
1. Added missing 'using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;' to ShellTests.cs, WToastTests.cs and WSidebarTests.cs (Services.AddSingleton is an extension method that needs the namespace imported per-file; it happened to already be present in the base WakeelTestContext.cs, masking the gap until those files tried to call it themselves).
2. Fixed ShellTests.cs's 'Components.WSidebar' / 'Components.WTopBar' / 'Components.WSidebar.Keys.Attention' references, which were resolving to the nested test namespace 'Wakeel.UI.Tests.Components' instead of 'Wakeel.UI.Components' (CS0234); added 'using Wakeel.UI.Components;' and dropped the now-redundant prefix.
3. Set 'JSInterop.Mode = Bunit.JSRuntimeMode.Loose;' in the shared WakeelTestContext base class — bunit 2.11.3's BunitContext defaults to Strict mode, which was throwing JSRuntimeUnhandledInvocationException on every JS interop call the shell makes (theme application on ThemeService.Initialize/SetTheme, WDialog's focus-trap wiring), even though several tests legitimately assert against those same recorded invocations.
4. Rewrote ShellTests.Gallery_Renders_UnderMainLayout_WithoutThrowing to actually render Gallery inside MainLayout (it previously rendered Gallery standalone, so the title it publishes via PageHeaderState — which MainLayout's header row displays — never appeared in the markup being asserted on).
5. Fixed a real component bug in WBreadcrumb.razor: it only rendered non-last crumbs as a clickable <button> when an OnClick delegate happened to be wired, whereas breadcrumb semantics (and the test coverage) call for every non-current crumb to render as a button regardless of whether a handler is attached (EventCallback.InvokeAsync on an unset delegate is a safe no-op).

After these fixes: dotnet build src/Wakeel.UI, dotnet build src/Wakeel.Desktop, and dotnet build+test tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests all report 0 warnings / 0 errors, with 127/127 bUnit tests passing (well above the ≥40 requirement). I did not touch Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props, Wakeel.slnx, or anything under Wakeel.Core, and made no git commits — everything is left in the working tree per instructions.
